name: In-the-Money Covered Call
summary: Covered call written at a strike below spot, trading upside for a large downside cushion and a high probability of a small, defined gain.
max_profit: (strike - share price + credit) x 100 - a small number, achieved as long as the stock stays above the strike

greeks.theta: strongly positive relative to the small max profit

when_to_use: When the system wants share exposure with a large cushion, in high IV, on a range-bound or mildly declining underlying, or as a way to hold a core ETF position defensively.
entry_rules: Require credit such that downside cushion (spot - breakeven)/spot >= 5%.
Strike chosen by delta in [0.60, 0.75]; never deeper than 0.80 delta (extrinsic collapses and assignment becomes near-certain).
Require extrinsic value of the short call >= 0.5% of spot at entry, else the trade earns nothing.
management_rules: Close at 50-60% of the extrinsic captured, not of total premium (intrinsic is not profit).
At 21 DTE, roll down-and-out only if the stock has fallen below the strike; otherwise let it be called in a controlled close.
If the stock rallies well above the strike, do nothing - max profit is already locked; just do not get assigned early around a dividend.
exit_rules: HARD: this call will almost always be ITM. Buy it back and sell the shares as one combo no later than 15:30 ET on expiration day, or earlier when extrinsic < 0.05.
Extrinsic monitor runs continuously: if call extrinsic < 0.05, unwind the unit that session.
Ex-dividend: unwind the unit before the close the day prior to ex-date unless extrinsic > 1.10 x dividend.
assignment_risk: Very high by design - the call is ITM, so early assignment around ex-dividend is likely and expiration assignment is the default outcome. For a system that must never be assigned, this strategy demands the tightest extrinsic monitor of the whole family.
buying_power: Shares only; the ITM call reduces net capital at risk because of the large credit.
liquidity_needs: ITM calls are wider; require spread <= 6% of extrinsic value, not of mid, and OI >= 250.
common_mistakes: Treating intrinsic value as income; going deeper than 0.80 delta and earning essentially nothing while carrying full share downside; ignoring the near-certain assignment.
zero_dte_notes: A 0DTE ITM covered call is just a share sale with extra steps and near-certain assignment. Do not automate.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
